name: Commercial Hydraulics & Fluid Power Systems
headline: Marketing for
intro: Help customers find your hydraulic repair and fluid power services. We build ads and pages that explain what you repair, where you work and how to reach your team.
challenges: The wrong calls take time
Broad repair ads can bring requests for equipment or areas you do not cover.
Urgent repairs and rebuilds get mixed up
A broken hose needs a quick call. A cylinder rebuild may need more detail before you can quote.
Your service area is unclear
Buyers need to know where you work and when someone can respond.
playbook: Focus the ads
Choose searches for the repairs you offer and the places you serve.
Explain the repair service
Show the equipment you work on, your hours and how to reach the right team.
Ask a few useful questions
Get the location, equipment type and urgency before asking for more detail.
Review the calls
Record whether the request was a fit and whether it became a job.
capabilities: Repair work at the customer’s site.
Workshop repairs and quotes for worn cylinders.
Service for the pumps and motors you support.
Planned work to keep factory and fleet equipment running.
scenario: An equipment owner searches for hydraulic hose repair nearby.
A page shows your service area, hours and phone number.
Your team gets the job location and equipment details, then checks whether you can help.
faqs: Can you focus ads on our service area?
Yes. We use the areas you actually cover and check where the calls come from.
Can we promote both repairs and rebuilds?
Yes. Each needs its own page and next step. A repair call can go to your service desk, while rebuild requests go to the person who prepares quotes.
description: Marketing for hydraulic repair and fluid power companies. Help customers find your services, check your coverage and ask for a repair or rebuild quote.

buyer_brief.decision: A hose failure may need help today. A workshop rebuild may start with a quote. Keep those requests separate so buyers reach the right person.
buyer_brief.page: The repair page should show hours and coverage. The rebuild page should explain what parts you work on and what details you need to quote.
buyer_brief.handoff: Check whether the job is in your area and fits your services. Review urgent calls separately from planned workshop work.

name: Specialized Attachment Manufacturers & Dealers
headline: Marketing for
intro: Help buyers find the right attachment and understand what it fits. We build ads and pages for attachment makers and dealers, with clear product details and a simple way to ask for a quote.
challenges: The attachment may not fit
Buyers need to check the machine model and job before choosing a product.
General searches bring the wrong requests
Not every attachment search matches the brands or types you sell.
Quote requests miss key details
Your team needs to know the machine, intended use and delivery location.
playbook: Group products clearly
Create useful pages for the attachment types you sell.
Show fit and uses
Use accurate product details and explain which jobs each attachment is made for.
Make quotes easier
Ask for the machine model, job and buying timeline.
Check the requests
Review whether buyers need a product you can supply.
capabilities: Tools for breaking, cutting and demolition work.
Attachments for clearing trees and brush.
Tools for digging and moving soil.
Attachments built for a specific machine or job.
scenario: An owner searches for an attachment for their excavator.
A product page explains its uses and the details needed to check fit.
Your sales team receives the machine model and job details before discussing a quote.
faqs: Can you help buyers check compatibility?
We can make your approved fit information easier to find. Your team should confirm that a product suits the machine and job.
Can we separate dealer and customer requests?
Yes. Clear links and form choices help send each request to the right person.
description: Marketing for attachment makers and equipment dealers. Explain product fit, reach buyers through search and make quote requests easier.

buyer_brief.decision: A product name alone is not enough to check fit. Buyers should share their machine model and the work they plan to do.
buyer_brief.page: Group pages by attachment type and use. Show approved fit details, then give buyers a clear way to ask about a purchase or rental.
buyer_brief.handoff: Check the product, machine and buying plans before counting a request as a good fit.

name: Commercial Fleet Graphics & Industrial Wraps
headline: Marketing for
intro: Help businesses find your fleet graphics and vehicle wrap services. We make it easier to explain the work, show real examples and collect the details needed for a quote.
challenges: Personal wraps and fleet jobs get mixed up
Business fleets often need a different plan from a single personal vehicle.
Buyers cannot see how a rollout works
They need to understand design, installation locations and scheduling.
Quotes start with too little detail
Vehicle count, types and dates affect the work and price.
playbook: Focus on business fleets
Use ads and page copy that make your commercial services clear.
Show real examples
Use approved photos to show the vehicles and types of work you handle.
Explain the steps
Describe how design, approval and installation work.
Keep quotes moving
Record the next step and follow up when the customer is ready.
capabilities: Graphics for vans, trucks and delivery vehicles.
Branding for vehicles used by field crews.
Graphics for machines and other large equipment.
Vehicle graphics for public services and transit.
scenario: A fleet manager looks for a company to wrap several vans.
A page shows examples and explains how installation is scheduled.
The request includes vehicle count, locations and target dates so your team can prepare a quote.
faqs: Can we focus on fleet work instead of personal vehicles?
Yes. We make that focus clear in your ads, pages and quote questions.
What should the first quote form ask?
Start with vehicle types, how many there are, where they are based and when the work is needed. Detailed artwork can follow later.
description: Marketing for fleet graphics and wrap companies. Show your work, explain installation plans and help businesses request a quote.

buyer_brief.decision: A fleet job may involve many vehicles and several locations. The buyer needs to know how you would plan the work.
buyer_brief.page: Show real examples and explain where you install. Ask for vehicle count, locations, artwork status and dates.
buyer_brief.handoff: Keep fleet requests separate from personal wraps. Track each job through design approval, quote and installation.

name: Modular Buildings, Site Offices & Blast-Resistant Modules
headline: Marketing for
intro: Help customers find your modular buildings and site offices. We explain rental and purchase options clearly, so buyers can ask about space that fits their site and schedule.
challenges: Rental and purchase needs differ
A short site job and a long-term building need different information.
Delivery details are missing
Location, site access and required dates all matter.
Building options are hard to compare
Buyers need clear details about size, use and what is included.
playbook: Separate rental and purchase
Give each option a clear page and next step.
Explain the building options
Show the types, uses and sizes you can supply.
Ask about the site
Collect location, quantity and delivery dates before preparing a quote.
Track the next step
Keep site discussions, quotes and follow-up dates together.
capabilities: Space for work, breaks and daily staff needs.
Buildings for site security and entry points.
Units with features such as blast resistance, where your business supplies them.
Several units planned together for a larger site.
scenario: A contractor searches for a site office rental.
A page explains unit options, delivery areas and how to ask about availability.
Your team receives the site location, number of units and required dates.
faqs: Can we advertise rentals and building sales?
Yes. Separate pages help each buyer find the right details and contact route.
Can the form confirm delivery or site suitability?
No. It collects the starting details. Your team still needs to check access, availability and site requirements.
description: Marketing for modular building and site office suppliers. Explain rental and purchase options, delivery areas and how to ask for a quote.

buyer_brief.decision: A temporary office may be needed quickly. A permanent building may need more planning and approval. Keep the two paths clear.
buyer_brief.page: Show rental periods, building uses and delivery areas. Ask about the site and dates, then let your team check the details.
buyer_brief.handoff: Record whether the buyer wants to rent or buy. Track the site discussion, quote and final decision.

name: Material Handling, Forklifts & Automated Guided Vehicles
headline: Marketing for
intro: Help buyers find your forklifts, rentals and repair services. We build clear pages for each part of the business, so customers can explain what they need and reach the right team.
challenges: Different requests reach the same inbox
A repair call and a new forklift quote need different responses.
Buyers may not know the right model
They may only know the load, lift height and space they work in.
Rental dates are missing
Your team needs the location and rental period to check availability.
playbook: Separate sales, rentals and repairs
Give each service its own page and form or phone contact.
Explain the equipment
Use accurate details about capacity and the jobs each type supports.
Ask about the work
Collect load needs, location and dates to help your team check fit.
Review each service separately
Compare repair calls with repair calls, and rental requests with rentals.
capabilities: Equipment for purchase or longer-term lease.
Equipment for temporary or seasonal needs.
Help buyers compare electric equipment for their fleet.
Vehicles and systems that move goods with less manual driving.
scenario: A warehouse manager searches for a forklift rental.
A rental page explains the options and asks about the job.
Your team gets the load needs, site location and dates before checking availability.
faqs: Can we promote sales, rentals and service together?
Yes, with separate ads and pages where needed. Each request should reach the team that handles it.
Should the form recommend a forklift?
The form can collect useful details. Your equipment team should check which machine suits the job.
description: Marketing for forklift and material handling companies. Help buyers find your sales, rental and repair services and reach the right team.

buyer_brief.decision: Someone who needs a repair today has different questions from someone buying a forklift. Make each service easy to find.
buyer_brief.page: Give sales, rentals and repairs their own pages. Ask what the buyer needs to move, where they work and when they need help.
buyer_brief.handoff: Check equipment fit, dates and service coverage. Review each business line on its own before comparing results.

name: Commercial Generators & Critical Power Infrastructure
headline: Marketing for
intro: Help customers find your generator sales, installations and service work. We make it easier to explain what you support and guide each request to the right person.
challenges: Urgent calls and planned projects differ
A power problem needs a quick response. A new installation needs a longer discussion.
Broad searches bring unsuitable work
Home generator searches may not fit a commercial power business.
Project details arrive too late
Facility type, location and timing help your team decide how to respond.
playbook: Focus on the work you offer
Separate service, maintenance and installation ads.
Explain your coverage
Show the sites, equipment and areas your team supports.
Ask about the need
Get the location, type of site and project stage.
Follow the request
Track service calls separately from quotes for larger projects.
capabilities: Generator systems for the sites you support.
Rental power for projects and short-term needs.
Repairs and planned service for supported equipment.
Power systems that help a site keep running when its main supply is unavailable.
scenario: A facility manager searches for a generator service company.
A page shows the equipment you support and your service area.
Your team gets the site details and urgency before arranging the next step.
faqs: Can we separate urgent calls from new projects?
Yes. Use a clear phone route for service and a separate form for planned work.
Can the website tell buyers what power system they need?
It can explain your services and collect details. Your qualified team should assess the site and recommend the system.
description: Marketing for generator and power companies. Help buyers understand your sales, rentals and service work, then get in touch.

buyer_brief.decision: A breakdown, maintenance plan and new installation need different next steps. Make those choices clear before the buyer contacts you.
buyer_brief.page: Show service hours and coverage for repairs. For projects, ask about the site, stage and known requirements.
buyer_brief.handoff: Record whether each request reached the right team and led to a site visit, quote or job.

name: Custom CNC Machining, Precision Tooling & Contract Fabricators
headline: Marketing for
intro: Help buyers understand what your machine shop or fabrication business can do. We build pages around your processes, materials and job types, with a clear way to ask for a quote.
goal: Requests for machining and fabrication quotes
challenges: Your services are hard to find
A general overview may hide the process or material a buyer needs.
Quote requests do not fit the shop
The part size, material or order quantity may be outside your range.
Files arrive without enough context
Drawings alone may not explain the quantity, timing or type of work.
playbook: Show what the shop does
Create clear pages for your main processes and materials.
Use real examples
Share approved photos and job details that help buyers understand your work.
Improve quote questions
Ask about material, quantity and dates before arranging drawing transfer.
Review the results
Track which requests fit your shop and move on to quotes or orders.
capabilities: Machine work for parts within your size and material range.
Custom tools and molds your shop can make.
Cutting, forming, welding and related work.
Finishing parts and putting components together.
scenario: An engineer searches for a shop to make a batch of parts.
A page explains your processes, materials and job sizes.
The quote request gives your team the material, quantity and deadline. Drawings follow through an agreed method.
faqs: Can we focus on certain processes or materials?
Yes. We build pages and ads around the work your shop wants and can handle.
Do buyers need to upload a drawing right away?
Not always. Start with the job details. Agree on how to share drawings when your team is ready to review them.
description: Marketing for CNC machine shops and fabricators. Explain your processes and materials, show your work and make it easier to ask for a quote.

buyer_brief.decision: Buyers may compare processes, materials, part size and order volume before asking for a price. Clear details help them judge whether your shop fits.
buyer_brief.page: Show the work you can handle. Ask for the process, material, quantity and dates, then arrange a suitable way to receive drawings.
buyer_brief.handoff: Keep prototype requests separate from repeat orders. Record which jobs fit, which receive quotes and which become orders.

name: Heavy Haul, Rigging & Specialized Transportation
headline: Marketing for
intro: Help customers find your heavy haul, machinery moving and rigging services. We explain the work and routes you cover, and ask for the details your team needs to review a move.
challenges: General freight calls waste time
Not every load or route fits your equipment and services.
Load details are missing
Size, weight and access affect how your team reviews the move.
Buyers cannot judge your range
They need to know which types of machinery and projects you handle.
playbook: Focus on suitable moves
Use ads for your services and the routes you cover.
Explain the work you handle
Show approved project examples and equipment details.
Ask about the load
Collect pickup, destination, known size and weight, and dates.
Keep track of the quote
Record the site review, quote and follow-up steps.
capabilities: Transport for large loads on the routes you support.
Moving and positioning machines at a site.
Lifting jobs within your team’s services.
Planned moves involving several machines or work areas.
scenario: A plant manager searches for a machinery mover.
A page explains the moves you handle and the details needed for a quote.
Your team gets the route, load details and dates before reviewing the job.
faqs: Can ads focus on our usual routes?
Yes. We use the routes and areas you serve, then review whether the requests fit.
Does the quote form confirm that we can do the move?
No. It starts the discussion. Your operations team still needs to check the load, sites and requirements.
description: Marketing for heavy haul and rigging companies. Explain the loads and routes you cover and collect the details needed to review a move.

buyer_brief.decision: A machinery move needs more than a pickup address. Buyers should share what is moving, where it is going and when.
buyer_brief.page: Show the moves and routes you support. Collect known load and access details without promising a price before review.
buyer_brief.handoff: Check route and load fit, record any site visit, then follow the quote through to a decision.

challenges: Small repair searches miss your market

Specialist work is hard to explain
Buyers need clear details about the sites and systems you support.
Projects are at different stages

playbook: Focus on the right facilities
Build pages and ads for the site types you serve.
Explain your services
Describe your work using accurate details from your team.
Show real projects
Use approved photos and examples to explain how you work.
Ask about the project stage
Collect the site type, location, system details and timing.
capabilities: Cooling systems for storage and distribution buildings.
Cold storage for medicines, where your team has the required skills.
Service and upgrade work within your approved range.
scenario: A facility team looks for help with a cold storage expansion.
A page explains your services and shows approved project examples.
Your team receives the facility type, location and project stage before an initial discussion.
faqs: Can we avoid domestic repair requests?

Use accurate descriptions and approved examples. Have your team check statements about systems, qualifications and the work you can do.
description: Marketing for industrial refrigeration companies. Explain your services, show approved projects and help facility teams get in touch.

buyer_brief.decision: Repairs, upgrades and new cold storage projects may involve different people and deadlines. Each should have a clear contact route.
buyer_brief.page: Explain the sites and systems you support. Ask about the location, existing setup and project stage before a deeper discussion.
buyer_brief.handoff: Check whether the facility and work fit your services. Track site reviews and quotes over time, since larger projects may take months.

name: Pre-Engineered Steel Buildings & Rigid Frame Structures
headline: Marketing for
intro: Help buyers understand your steel building services. We make it clear whether you supply building packages, put them up or handle both, so customers can send a useful quote request.
challenges: Price questions lack detail
Size alone is not enough to quote a building. Use, location and included work matter.
Supply and installation get confused
Buyers may not know which parts of the project your business handles.
Project details come in slowly
A few clear questions can save repeated calls about the basics.
playbook: Explain the building uses
Show the types of buildings and projects you support.
Be clear about your role
List what your quote includes and what the buyer arranges separately.
Ask for the basics
Collect use, location, rough size and target dates.
Follow up at the right time
Keep track of the buyer’s plans and what they need next.
capabilities: Steel building packages for business use.
Structures for storage and industrial work.
Open-span buildings for farms and related businesses.
Building frames and clearly defined installation work.
scenario: A business owner searches for a steel warehouse supplier.
A page explains building options and what your service includes.
The request gives your team the use, location and rough size before an estimate.
faqs: Do we need to show instant prices?
Only if you can keep them accurate and explain what is included. Otherwise, a clear quote request is a better starting point.
Can we make it clear that we only supply the building?
Yes. State that on the page and in the form so buyers understand your role before asking for a quote.
description: Marketing for steel building suppliers and contractors. Explain what your service includes and help buyers send a useful quote request.

buyer_brief.decision: Buyers need to know whether you supply the package, erect the building or do both. Make that clear before discussing price.
buyer_brief.page: Ask for the intended use, location, rough size and dates. Explain which work is included in your service.
buyer_brief.handoff: Keep early planning questions separate from projects ready for a quote. Record what the estimating team needs next.

Equipment needs spread across several stages of a job.

faqs: Can requests go to the right branch?

Keep track of questions, technical reviews and follow-up dates.
capabilities: Robot-based work areas for supported tasks.

buyer_brief.handoff: Track whether the project fits, what has been reviewed and who needs to respond. Record why a project is delayed or does not go ahead.
